title: Chandra resolves ASASSN-14ko: its X-ray nucleus faded tenfold by 2022, the mid-2022 cycle gave no dip time, and UV peaks imply period decay only because the flares became wider
abstract: Question: campaign studies found a constant 108.44-d soft X-ray dip clock for ASASSN-14ko in 2020-2024 (a stall of the period decrease), but no X-ray marker exists for cycles 25-29 (2022-2023), and Swift UVW2 peaks alone still show the old decrease. Swift XRT and NICER do not resolve the two nuclei of the host. Approach: we reduced all 13 public Chandra ACIS-S observations (2020-2023; nine bracket cycle 26 in 2022 May-June) without CIAO, separated the northern nucleus (ASASSN-14ko) from the south-west nucleus 1.6 arcsec away with a two-source PSF likelihood in four astrometric variants plus an astrometry-free summed aperture, compared cycle 26 with the XRT+NICER dips of all other cycles, and measured how flare markers move with the optical rise width. Results: (1) between 2021 January and 2022 May the nucleus faded by a factor 13-16 in 2-7 keV (range 12-30) and 7.5-8 in 0.5-2 keV, while the south-west nucleus changed by 0.74. (2) In cycle 26 the nucleus was below its pre-dip level L 1.9 d before the clock (0.14-0.62 L, p = 2e-8 to 0.011), but the depth and the state 2.5 d after the clock (0.27-1.12 L) depend on the astrometry, and the summed emission stayed near the pre-dip scatter; thus no dip time can be measured. (3) A soft X-ray outburst of 16-17 L (summed 8.9-fold) occurred 6.8 d after the clock, at the UV peak, and decayed within a day; no other cycle exceeds 1.8 L in this phase except cycle 28 (7 L). (4) The UVW2 peak moves +0.36 +/- 0.06 d per day of g rise width and the half-rise -1.13 +/- 0.15; in 2022-2023 the rise width grew to 12-15 d. (5) UV peaks alone prefer the Payne et al. curvature by Delta(-2 ln L) = 13.8; with a rise-width term the curvature is -0.02 (95%: -0.48 to +0.40). Any X-ray/UV mixture with X-ray weight >= 0.3 prefers a constant period by Delta >= 5. Conclusion: the stall does not depend on the marker type; the UV disagreement is a flare-width effect. But the X-ray clock has a five-cycle gap in which the corona was ten times fainter, dips were shallow or early, and X-ray outbursts occurred near the UV peak; stall models must allow for these changes. Limitations: no effective-area responses (soft fading includes contamination change); 1.6-arcsec source split depends on 0.5-arcsec astrometry; marker tests use 7-10 cycles and were chosen after seeing the data; no public data cover the 2026 flares.

display.caption: Cycle 26 (2022): Chandra rates of the resolved northern nucleus (four astrometric treatments), the south-west nucleus and both together; Swift UVW2 with the UV-peak posterior; ASAS-SN g. A partial decline before the clock time, no measurable dip time, and an X-ray outburst at the UV peak.
Chandra 2020-2023: the northern nucleus (ASASSN-14ko) faded by a factor 13-16 in 2-7 keV and about 8 in 0.5-2 keV between 2021 January and 2022 May; the south-west nucleus stayed steady.
Period test against the X-ray weight of a mixed X-ray/UV marker: UV peaks alone prefer the published decrease, every mixture with X-ray weight 0.3 or more prefers a constant period.
